content: Assessment question: in InnoDB MVCC, what role does a Read View play when deciding whether a row version is visible to a transaction?
I know it is related to snapshots, but can you explain what a Read View actually contains before I answer?

A Read View is the snapshot metadata used to decide which transaction versions are visible; it tracks active transaction boundaries and is combined with row version metadata/undo chains. In READ COMMITTED a new Read View is generally created for each consistent read, while in REPEATABLE READ the transaction normally reuses the first consistent-read view. Let me ask you with that in mind: why does this create repeatable reads?
Then RR can reuse the same visibility boundary, so a transaction keeps seeing the same eligible committed versions even if another transaction commits later.
